reviewed_by: worker-6 source re-review from worker-5 packet notes plus primary XML/PDF
extraction_scope: Mechanism ontology rebuilt to avoid automated keyword overclaiming; direct mechanisms are limited to observed fungal uptake/localization assays, while antiviral mode remains phenotypic/speculative.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PAFB and PAF in susceptible fungi
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Fungal toxicity is associated with uptake/internalization of BODIPY-labelled PAFB or PAF and PI-positive loss of viability in susceptible fungal cells.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Association of uptake with toxicity is direct for fungal cells, but exact molecular intracellular target remains unresolved.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BODIPY-PAFB internalization depends on active cellular metabolism because NaN3, CCCP, and low temperature blocked uptake while untreated cells showed vacuolar localization.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay supports active uptake/metabolism dependence, not a named receptor or downstream lethal target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NMR analysis supports a compact beta-folded structure stabilized by three intramolecular disulfide bonds with an abcabc pattern.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural evidence supports fold/stability context but is not by itself a killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PAFB and PAF against HCoV-229E in L132 cells
mechanism_claims.claim_text: PAFB and PAF reduce HCoV-229E cytopathogenic effect and viral immunofluorescence signal at 8 µM, but the source frames the antiviral mode as unresolved.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not classify as direct virucidal, entry, replication, or host-metabolism mechanism; the paper explicitly leaves antiviral mode under investigation.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Antiviral effect is source-supported phenotypically, but direct mechanism is not resolved locally.
